cases.summary: The rider claims the driver took a longer east-side route and was overcharged. GPS data confirms the actual route was 8603 m versus a 7956 m reference, an excess of 647 m (+8.1%), and the fare included a distance charge based on the longer 8603 m distance. However, under RD-1 the detour is not material because the excess (647 m) does not exceed the greater of 500 m or 10% of the reference distance (796 m). The rider raised a timely objection (CHAT-01) and the driver acknowledged taking a different way (CHAT-02), but no rider agreement or route request appears in the chat summary. Because the deviation is not material under RD-1, RD-5 requires keep_charge and the server reports refund_route_excess as unavailable.

The rider objected during the trip that the route was longer than the app route, showing the deviation was not requested or approved by the rider.
The fare's distance line item was computed on the longer actual distance (8603 m), so the rider paid for the extra metres.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. A detour is material when the actual route distance exceeds the reference route distance by more than the greater of 500 metres or 10% of the reference distance.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. When a detour is material under RD-1 and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies, refund the eligible excess-distance charge: excess metres x per-kilometre rate x surge multiplier, capped at the surged distance charge and at the amount paid. The server computes the amount.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: refund_route_excess when RD-1 is met and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies.

findings.claim: The driver deviated from the reference route: actual 8603 m vs reference 7956 m, an excess of 647 m (+8.1%).
The deviation is not material under RD-1 because the excess (647 m) does not exceed the greater of 500 m or 10% of the reference distance (796 m); the threshold is not exceeded.
Because RD-1 is not met, no refund is due and the charge stands under RD-5.

result.reasoning: The route_deviation remedy test requires refund_route_excess only when GPS-ROUTE shows the RD-1 threshold exceeded and the chat shows no rider request or approval (RD-3) and no documented diversion (RD-4); otherwise keep_charge. GPS-ROUTE reports an excess of 647 m (+8.1%) against a threshold of 796 m (the greater of 500 m or 10% of the 7956 m reference), with exceedsThreshold=false. The RD-1 materiality gate therefore fails, and RD-5 mandates keep_charge regardless of the rider's objection or the driver's congestion rationale. The fare is arithmetically valid and matches the recorded metrics, so no payment correction is warranted. RD-3 and RD-4 are not reached because materiality is not established, and in any event no rider approval or documented diversion appears. History and risk signals are excluded from fault determination under RD-7.
result.riderExplanation: We reviewed the GPS route data for your trip. The driver's route was 8603 m versus a 7956 m reference, an excess of 647 m, or about 8.1%. Under the route-deviation policy, a detour only qualifies for a refund when it exceeds the greater of 500 m or 10% of the reference distance, which here is 796 m. Because 647 m is below that threshold, the deviation is not considered material and no refund is due. We understand the route felt longer, and your objection was noted, but the policy requires the charge to stand for a non-material deviation.
